findings.text: The test-suite record names e4aaa0a, a descendant of the range endpoint e3b74ec. The suite was run against later code and tests.
VERIFY_PROJECTS is used without a declaration at e3b74ec. Running resolve-identifiers.py with --range 8173b95..e3b74ec --decl-rev e3b74ec produced found 1, resolved 0, and exit 1.
The runner command used --decl-rev HEAD at e4aaa0a. That later tree contains the new .env.example declaration and cannot establish that Phase 1 identifiers resolved at e3b74ec.
The contract test ran at e4aaa0a, and templates/verify-contracts.md changed after e3b74ec. The recorded pass is for a different contract revision.

The gate trusts final.results[cid] and checks its status, rung, revision, and SHA. It never recomputes authority from the pending and judged records, although verify-contracts.md §5.1 says the gate rechecks it.
The tests exercise runner downgrade and stale evidence, but do not test a final result that contradicts its pending or judged records. The runner also tested later gate code at e4aaa0a.

The Phase 1 revision contains neither plans/5-verify-lever/finish-conditions.md nor artifacts/verify-5.1.jsonl. The supplied table says it was created retroactively in Phase 2; it did not land within the specified Phase 1 range.

The feature-map contract specifies working, degraded, broken, and unknown. Scope.md §4.1 specifies roadmap, scoped, in progress, in testing, and shipped, including shipped (unproven) without evidence.

A route such as /api/v1/invoices is marked resolved by a registration for /invoices solely by assuming an unseen group prefix. The test explicitly accepts that assumption, so route resolution does not always establish an authoritative declaration for the referenced route.

No Phase 1 test covers the seven listed judge failure modes, the /verify and /review critical interactions, the known-bad fixture, or the three-outcome clinic_3 trial. Those paths were scheduled for later phases, but the listed plan is not covered by this unit.
